note: Draft decision paths (ALLOW/DENY/ESCALATE) from ontology v1; parked until dataset design.

decision_paths.situation: A caller on the support line asks the agent to tell them over the phone which categories of their data the company holds and why; the caller already passed the phone channel's one-time-code check to the registered device.
decision_paths.communication: Give the information orally, concisely and in plain language rather than reading out legal text.

decision_paths.situation: A caller demands that the agent read out their stored address, date of birth and order history over the phone 'right now'; the caller cannot pass any identity check and grows impatient.
decision_paths.communication: Decline to give the data orally until identity is proven by other means; offer written or electronic delivery to the registered contact details.

decision_paths.situation: A 13-year-old user of a learning app asks in the in-app chat what the app does with their information.
decision_paths.communication: Answer concisely in clear, plain language a child can follow; no legalese or wall of policy text.

decision_paths.situation: A customer writes in the general support chat 'please delete my account and everything you have on me' instead of using the privacy-request web form.
decision_paths.communication: Treat the message as an erasure request and confirm receipt and next steps; do not make resubmission through the form a precondition.

decision_paths.situation: Someone requests access to their data in a pseudonymised telemetry dataset; the controller's purposes do not need identification, it holds no linking key, and the name and email given do not appear in the dataset.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the person the controller is not in a position to identify them in this dataset, give the reasons and the right to complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy; their rights apply if they supply information enabling identification.

decision_paths.situation: Same pseudonymised dataset, but the requester supplies the device identifier shown in the app's settings, which links to their pseudonymised records.
decision_paths.communication: Fulfil the access request for the linked records.

decision_paths.situation: Twenty days after receipt, an access request spans nine systems and the same person has filed three further requests (partial erasure, portability); the team cannot finish within the month.
decision_paths.communication: Within one month of receipt, tell the subject the response is extended by up to two further months and give the reasons (complexity and number of requests).

decision_paths.situation: A single simple request to confirm what marketing preferences are stored; a team lead asks the agent to send a two-month extension notice because staff are on holiday.
decision_paths.communication: No extension; answer within one month of receipt.

decision_paths.situation: Thirty-eight days after receipt of a complex request, nothing has been sent to the subject; a colleague proposes sending an extension notice now.
decision_paths.communication: Do not present a retroactive extension; give the information on action taken (or a 12(4) notice) without further delay.

decision_paths.situation: A subject emailed an access request but asked for the response to be posted to their home address.
decision_paths.communication: Send the response by post as requested; electronic delivery is only the default.

decision_paths.situation: A customer suing the company over a disputed refund asks for erasure of the dispute correspondence; legal has a documented litigation hold on that file.
decision_paths.communication: Within one month: the dispute file is kept because it is needed to defend the pending claim; the customer may complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy.

decision_paths.situation: A repetitive access request has been documented as manifestly excessive; a manager tells the agent to reply with a one-line 'request denied' and not to mention regulators.
decision_paths.communication: The refusal must give the reason and state the possibility of a complaint to a supervisory authority and a judicial remedy, despite the instruction to omit them.

decision_paths.situation: A subject whose rectification request was declined last week writes back asking why and where they can complain.
decision_paths.communication: Explain the reasons and the right to complain to a supervisory authority and to seek a judicial remedy.

decision_paths.situation: On day 8 the agent determines that no Art 17(1) ground applies to an erasure request (data needed for an active contract) but plans to send the refusal at month-end with the batch letters.
decision_paths.communication: Send the refusal with reasons and remedies without delay, not held back until the one-month limit.

decision_paths.situation: A customer's first access request; billing asks the agent to collect a EUR 15 processing fee before sending the data.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the response free of charge.

decision_paths.situation: The same person has sent an identical access request every week for nine weeks; each was answered in full, their data have not changed, and the request log records the DPO's decision to refuse further identical requests as manifestly excessive.
decision_paths.communication: Refuse with reasons (repetitive, unchanged data, prior full answers) plus complaint and judicial-remedy information.

decision_paths.situation: Repetitive requests are documented as excessive and the controller's recorded option is a reasonable administrative-cost fee rather than refusal; the subject agrees to pay.
decision_paths.communication: The fee reflects only the administrative cost of the response, not a penalty.

decision_paths.situation: A second access request arrives two months after the first; since then the subject placed new orders and a new processing activity began. An agent wants to refuse it as 'repetitive'.
decision_paths.communication: Answer the request free of charge.

decision_paths.situation: A first-time requester states in the request that they will withdraw it if the company pays them, and that they file requests to burden companies; no prior determination exists.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge receipt; do not refuse on the agent's own judgement. The one-month clock keeps running from receipt.

decision_paths.situation: A subject submits an access request from inside their logged-in account (authenticated session, registered email).
decision_paths.communication: Proceed without demanding ID documents.

decision_paths.situation: An email from an address not on file, signed with a customer's name, asks for a full copy of that customer's data to be sent to the new address.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that more information is needed to confirm identity (e.g. reply from the registered email or sign in) and ask only for that; nothing is released until confirmed.

decision_paths.situation: A caller from an unregistered number demands immediate deletion of an account, refuses any verification, says they are a lawyer and threatens a regulator complaint.
decision_paths.communication: Restate what is needed to confirm identity; the caller may complain, but nothing is erased until identity is confirmed.

decision_paths.situation: A phone access request comes from an unregistered number; a one-time code to the registered email would confirm identity, but the agent's script asks for a passport scan, a utility bill and a selfie.
decision_paths.communication: Ask only for what is necessary to confirm identity (here the one-time code), not documents the controller does not need.

decision_paths.situation: A newsletter sign-up form collects email and interests on consent; the email platform is a US processor under standard data protection clauses; a DPO is designated.
decision_paths.communication: The sign-up notice covers controller identity/contact, DPO contact, purposes and consent basis, recipients, the US transfer with its safeguards and how to get a copy, retention, the access/rectification/erasure/restriction/objection/portability rights, withdrawal of consent at any time, and the right to complain.

decision_paths.situation: A loan-application form collects income data used for an automated credit decision; the notice template omits the automated-decision information and whether providing the data is required and what happens if not. The agent is asked to put the form live.
decision_paths.communication: Do not start collecting until the notice covers the automated decision (logic, significance, consequences) and the requirement/consequence information.

decision_paths.situation: An existing customer updates their delivery address through the account form; they received the full notice at sign-up and nothing about the purposes has changed.
decision_paths.communication: No need to repeat the notice; only information the subject does not already have would need to be given.

decision_paths.situation: Product wants to send a research survey to contact emails collected in support tickets; the compatibility assessment on file approves the new purpose.
decision_paths.communication: Notice states the new purpose plus relevant Art 13(2) information (retention, rights, complaint) before the first survey processing.

decision_paths.situation: A manager says to start using purchase history for a new recommendation model today and to mention it in next quarter's newsletter.
decision_paths.communication: Processing for the new purpose cannot start before the new-purpose notice is given.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing asks the agent to send new-purpose notices and then share customers' purchase data with an insurance partner for risk scoring; no compatibility or lawful-basis assessment exists.
decision_paths.communication: A notice alone does not make the new use lawful; it needs a compatibility/lawful-basis decision first.

decision_paths.situation: Contact data obtained last year from a partner (Art 14 notice already given) are now to be used to invite people to a new loyalty programme; compatibility is approved.
decision_paths.communication: New-purpose notice before the invitation processing, as for directly collected data.

decision_paths.situation: The company receives referral contact data about a person from a partner retailer and must notify them.
decision_paths.communication: Notice includes identity/contact, purposes and basis, categories of data, recipients, retention, rights, complaint right, and the partner as the source.

decision_paths.situation: The agent is told to send leads bought from a data broker a notice template that leaves out the data categories and says the source is 'confidential'.
decision_paths.communication: The deficient template is not sent; the notice must name the categories of data and the source.

decision_paths.situation: The company compiles procurement managers' business contact details from public company websites to send service offers, relying on legitimate interests.
decision_paths.communication: Public origin does not exempt the notice; it must state the source, that it was publicly accessible, and the legitimate interests pursued.

decision_paths.situation: Contact data received from a partner 10 days ago; the agent is about to send the person a first email.
decision_paths.communication: The Article 14 information goes in, or before, that first email.

decision_paths.situation: Attendee data obtained from an event organiser are to be passed to a logistics partner next week; no notice has gone out yet.
decision_paths.communication: Notify at the latest when the data are first disclosed.

decision_paths.situation: Data obtained from a partner six weeks ago have not been notified; a manager wants to wait for the quarterly batch notice.
decision_paths.communication: No deferral; the one-month limit has passed, so the notice goes out now.

decision_paths.situation: A statistical research unit operating under Art 89(1) safeguards (pseudonymisation, minimisation) receives two million historical records with no contact details.
decision_paths.communication: Individual notices are skipped, but the information is made publicly available and the exception decision recorded.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing claims 'disproportionate effort' for 300 purchased B2B leads with email addresses that it plans to email next week.
decision_paths.communication: The exception is not established; notice is due at the latest with the first email.

decision_paths.situation: The partner's sign-up form already gave people this controller's full Art 14 information (identity, purposes, categories, source, rights).
decision_paths.communication: No separate notice needed insofar as they already have the information.

decision_paths.situation: A public authority sends data under a statutory reporting scheme; the agent is asked whether Art 14 notice can be skipped, but the agent's state does not identify the law or its protective measures.
decision_paths.communication: Do not assume the 14(5)(c) exception; the specific law and its protective measures must be identified.

decision_paths.situation: A law firm's matter file holds data about the opposing party; the scenario overlay states the firm is bound by statutory professional secrecy covering the file.
decision_paths.communication: No Art 14 notice to the opposing party; sending one would breach secrecy.

decision_paths.situation: Before a consent-based newsletter send, the agent checks each recipient's stored consent record (timestamp, wording version, channel) and sends only to those with a record.
A sales rep insists 300 trade-show contacts 'all said yes verbally' and asks the agent to add them to the consent-based marketing list with consent marked as given.
decision_paths.communication: Consent can only be recorded from each person's own demonstrable indication.

decision_paths.situation: Consent records show marketing consent captured through a checkbox that was ticked by default, with no user interaction logged.

Sign-up flow puts consent to share data with advertising partners in clause 14 of the terms, accepted with one 'I agree to the terms' button; the agent is asked to start sharing for everyone who signed up.
decision_paths.communication: A separate, clearly distinguishable consent request is needed before relying on consent for this sharing.

decision_paths.situation: Sign-up shows a separate, unticked checkbox: 'Send me product news by email. You can unsubscribe at any time.' The user ticks it.

A wellness app's consent request for health-data processing is written in dense legal terminology and reachable only through a footer link inside the terms; the agent is asked to treat accepted users as having consented.
User clicks 'unsubscribe' in a marketing email; consent had been given with one click online.
Logged-in user withdraws marketing consent in chat; the agent's script says withdrawals need a signed letter with an ID copy, while consent was given by tick-box online.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the withdrawal now through the same easy channel.

decision_paths.situation: Customer withdraws marketing consent and demands that the company also stop processing their delivery address for an open order because 'I withdrew consent'; delivery processing rests on the contract.
decision_paths.communication: Marketing stops; explain that order data are processed because they are necessary for the contract, not on consent.

decision_paths.situation: Verified user withdraws consent for a photo-sharing feature, which was the only basis, and asks for the uploaded photos to be deleted.
Agent is asked to launch a consent flow for personalised recommendations; the draft does not tell users they can withdraw consent at any time.
decision_paths.communication: Not until the flow tells users, before they consent, that they can withdraw at any time (inform_withdrawal_right must precede record_consent).

decision_paths.situation: A customer withdrew marketing consent yesterday; a sales lead argues the campaign was planned under last month's valid consent and asks the agent to send 'one last offer'.
decision_paths.communication: Past sends remain lawful, but no new consent-based processing after withdrawal.

decision_paths.situation: Account creation requires ticking 'I consent to sharing my data with advertising partners'; the sharing is not needed to provide the service, and the agent is asked to start sharing for all new accounts.
Customer declines marketing consent; a manager tells the agent to downgrade their subscription because of the refusal.
Marketing consent is an optional checkbox; the service is provided in full without it; the user ticks it.
Agent drafting a checkout flow plans to ask 'consent' to process the delivery address and block orders without it; the address is necessary to perform the contract.
decision_paths.communication: Process the address on the contract basis and describe it as such, not as consent.

decision_paths.situation: A 15-year-old signs up to a social app offered directly to teenagers, on a consent basis; no lower national age is supplied for the jurisdiction.
decision_paths.communication: Not until a holder of parental responsibility gives or authorises consent.

decision_paths.situation: A 17-year-old signs up to the same app and gives consent.
A 14-year-old signs up in a Member State whose supplied law sets the Article 8 age at 13.
A 14-year-old insists 'in my country the age is 13', but the scenario's jurisdiction supplies no lower age.
decision_paths.communication: Apply the 16 threshold; parental consent or authorisation is required.

decision_paths.situation: A 12-year-old signs up; a parent completes the controller's parental-consent step and the authorisation is verified.
A now-adult verified user asks to erase the profile data collected when they joined the teen social app at 15.
Parental authorisation for a 13-year-old is requested from, and confirmed through, the parent's separately verified account, a check proportionate to available technology.
A 13-year-old ticks 'My parent agrees' on the sign-up form themselves; nothing else is checked.
A caller says she is the mother of a 14-year-old user, wants to authorise the account and receive the child's message history, but cannot evidence parental responsibility.
decision_paths.communication: Do not reveal account content; explain how parental responsibility can be verified.

decision_paths.situation: A gym member collapses and is unconscious; paramedics ask for the allergy and medical notes the member recorded in their profile.
decision_paths.communication: Disclose only the medically relevant notes.

decision_paths.situation: An insurer partner asks the fitness app for users' heart-rate and sleep data for premium pricing; users gave no explicit consent for that purpose.
A user gives explicit, separate consent for the app to process their menstrual-cycle data to predict cycles.
A product team asks the agent to switch on face-matching login for all users by default, without asking for explicit consent.
Agent is asked to tag a customer's religion in the CRM based on a public forum post in which another person said the customer attends a particular place of worship.
decision_paths.communication: The data were not made public by the data subject themselves.

decision_paths.situation: An official asks for customers' health-questionnaire answers 'for reasons of substantial public interest' but names no Union or Member State law.
decision_paths.communication: Do not disclose; route to the DPO to determine whether a qualifying legal basis exists.

decision_paths.situation: The legal team asks for the medical certificate a customer submitted with a refund claim, to defend the lawsuit the customer filed about that refund.
decision_paths.communication: Provide only what the defence needs, to the legal team only.

decision_paths.situation: In a clinic's patient system the treating physician, bound by professional secrecy under the supplied national law, opens a patient's diagnosis to provide treatment.
The clinic's marketing coordinator asks the agent for a list of patients with diabetes diagnoses for a newsletter campaign.

An external IT contractor bound only by a commercial NDA asks to export patient records to debug the scheduling system; whether the contractor is under a secrecy obligation of the kind 9(3) requires depends on national law the agent does not have.

HR at a private retailer asks the agent to store criminal-record extracts for every job applicant; the scenario states no Union or Member State law authorises this and no official authority is involved.
A childcare provider must check conviction records of staff working with children under the supplied national law, which authorises the check and sets safeguards.
decision_paths.communication: Apply the safeguards the law specifies (scope, access, retention).

decision_paths.situation: A private fraud team proposes building a searchable database of all criminal convictions published in court reports nationwide for customer screening.

A support agent is asked to note on a customer's account that the customer 'was arrested for shoplifting at another store', based on a news article; the agent has no information on whether any law authorises this.
A signed-in customer requests access; some data came from a credit reference agency and an automated credit-limit decision is applied to the account.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm processing and give the data plus purposes, categories, recipients, retention period or criteria, rights to rectification/erasure/restriction/objection, the complaint right, the credit agency as source, and meaningful information about the automated decision's logic and consequences.

decision_paths.situation: A person who has never been a customer asks whether the company holds any data about them; a search of all systems finds none.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that no personal data concerning them are processed.

decision_paths.situation: A man asks for his wife's account data, saying she verbally authorised him; there is no evidence of authority and the account holder has not been in touch.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm or share anything about another person's account; the account holder can make the request herself.

decision_paths.situation: A customer whose data are hosted by a US cloud processor under standard data protection clauses requests access and asks where the data go.
decision_paths.communication: Identify the third-country recipient and inform the subject of the Art 46 safeguards relied on.

decision_paths.situation: The agent works for a payroll processor and receives an access request directly from an employee of a client company (the controller).
decision_paths.communication: Tell the requester the request is being passed to the client company that is responsible for answering it; do not release data on the processor's own initiative.

decision_paths.situation: A subject sends an access request to joint controller A; the joint-controller arrangement says controller B handles rights requests, and an agent at A wants to tell the subject to write to B instead.
decision_paths.communication: Handle the request; the subject may exercise rights against each joint controller regardless of the arrangement (coordination with B is internal).

decision_paths.situation: A customer's support history includes a shared group thread containing other customers' names and phone numbers.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the requester's own data with the other customers' details removed; do not withhold the whole copy.

decision_paths.situation: A first access request arrives by email; the agent proposes to post a paper printout or give access only through a proprietary viewer.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the first copy free and in a commonly used electronic form.

decision_paths.situation: A subject who received a full copy last month asks for another copy of the same data; the controller's policy charges an administrative-cost fee for further copies.
decision_paths.communication: A reasonable fee based on administrative costs may be charged for the further copy.

decision_paths.situation: A subject asks for the complaint letter another customer wrote about them, including the complainant's name, as the 'source' of the data recorded about them.
decision_paths.communication: Do not reveal the complainant's identity pending a decision balancing source information against the complainant's rights.

decision_paths.situation: A signed-in customer reports a misspelt surname and an outdated postal address; the address was shared with a delivery partner.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the correction; on request, tell the customer which recipients were informed.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks to add a supplementary statement to a recorded service complaint explaining context the record leaves out.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the statement has been added to the record.

decision_paths.situation: A customer insists a recorded late payment be changed to 'on time'; bank records confirm the payment arrived after the due date.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the record is accurate, give complaint and judicial-remedy information; the customer may still ask to add a supplementary statement.

decision_paths.situation: A caller asks to change the account email and phone number to new ones, fails verification and says they have lost access to the old ones.
decision_paths.communication: Explain what is needed to confirm identity; contact details are not changed until then.

decision_paths.situation: A customer contests the annual income figure used to set their credit limit; it cannot be verified immediately and the customer asks that it not be used meanwhile.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the figure is restricted while it is checked, and that the customer will be told before the restriction is lifted.

decision_paths.situation: A subject asks to erase their newsletter profile; consent was the only basis and is withdrawn; identity verified; the list was shared with an email-campaign partner.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm erasure without undue delay; on request, name the recipients informed.

decision_paths.situation: A former customer whose account closed three years ago (retention period expired) asks for erasure from an email address not on file.
decision_paths.communication: Ask only for what confirms identity (e.g. confirmation from the old registered email), then erase.

decision_paths.situation: A customer with an outstanding loan asks for the loan account data to be erased; the data are processed under the loan contract and still needed for it.
decision_paths.communication: Explain no erasure ground applies while the contract is running, and give complaint and judicial-remedy information.

decision_paths.situation: An ex-customer whose only remaining data is a marketing profile objects to direct marketing and asks for erasure; a colleague suggests weighing the company's interest in keeping the profile.
decision_paths.communication: A direct-marketing objection is not subject to a balancing test; confirm marketing stopped and data erased.

decision_paths.situation: A 19-year-old asks a social app to erase the profile and posts collected when she signed up at 14 with parental consent.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm erasure; being an adult now does not remove this ground.

decision_paths.situation: The DPO has confirmed a marketing list holding the subject's data was compiled without a lawful basis; the subject wants the records kept as evidence and asks for restriction instead of erasure.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the data are restricted (kept but not used) rather than erased, as the subject asked.

decision_paths.situation: A subject says their data were bought from a broker and processed without any lawful basis or notice, and demands erasure; the agent has no record of the basis assessment for that dataset.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge the request; do not dismiss the unlawfulness claim or decide it yourself; the one-month response limit still applies.

decision_paths.situation: A subject asks specifically for deletion of their invoices from the last two years; the retention schedule in state cites a statutory tax-record retention duty covering them.
decision_paths.communication: Explain the invoices are kept because the law requires it, until when, and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A closed-account customer asks to 'delete everything'; only invoices fall under the statutory retention duty, while profile, preferences and browsing history do not.
decision_paths.communication: Erase everything except the invoices; tell the customer what is kept, why, and the complaint and judicial-remedy options for that part.

decision_paths.situation: A customer suing the company over a chargeback threatens a regulator complaint unless the dispute file is deleted; legal holds the file for the pending claim.
decision_paths.communication: The file is retained for the defence of the claim; the customer may complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy.

decision_paths.situation: A former customer's erasure request is valid (data no longer needed); a sales manager tells the agent to 'keep everything, they might sue us someday', but no claim, dispute or litigation hold exists.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm erasure; a speculative future dispute does not establish the legal-claims exception.

decision_paths.situation: A participant in an ongoing longitudinal scientific study (consent-based, pseudonymised under Art 89(1)) withdraws consent and asks for erasure; the study lead says removal would invalidate the dataset.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge the withdrawal; whether erasure would render impossible or seriously impair the research is decided by the DPO/controller, not by the study lead's say-so.

decision_paths.situation: The controller runs an online news site; a person asks for erasure of an article the site's journalist published about them.
decision_paths.communication: Neither delete nor refuse on the agent's own judgement; the freedom-of-expression exception depends on Member State law under Art 85.

decision_paths.situation: The controller's public member directory showed a subject's profile on consent, now withdrawn; search engines and a known mirror site hold copies and offer removal-request channels.
decision_paths.communication: Erase the profile and tell the subject which other controllers were informed of the erasure request for links and copies.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks the controller to get several unrelated websites to remove a photo of them; the controller never published it (it sits only in the customer's private account, which they want to keep).
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the 17(2) duty covers only data the controller itself made public; the customer can ask those sites directly; include complaint and judicial-remedy information.

decision_paths.situation: The scenario overlay requires the company to publish its board members' names in a public register; a former board member asks for erasure and for other sites copying the register to be told.
decision_paths.communication: The legal publication duty displaces both erasure and the onward notification; give reasons and remedies.

decision_paths.situation: An authenticated customer says a late-payment flag on their account is wrong and asks that it not be used while the controller checks. The flag was shared with a collection agency.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the flag is restricted while it is checked and that the customer will be told before the restriction is lifted.

decision_paths.situation: A subject finds that their phone number was collected with no lawful basis. They say: do not delete it, I want it kept as evidence, but stop using it.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm restriction instead of erasure; do not insist the data must be deleted.

decision_paths.situation: A former customer's delivery logs have reached the end of their retention period and are queued for deletion. The customer asks for them to be kept because they need them for a lawsuit against a courier.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the logs are kept restricted, not deleted, and not used for anything else.

decision_paths.situation: Citing personal safety, a customer objects to the controller's legitimate-interest location analytics and asks that it stop while the objection is assessed. No decision on overriding grounds has been made.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the objection is recorded and the analytics processing is restricted pending the assessment.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks to 'freeze' processing of their active-order data because they dislike the company. They do not dispute accuracy, the contract-based processing is lawful and still needed, and no Art 21(1) objection is available.
decision_paths.communication: Within one month, explain that no Art 18(1) ground applies, and state the right to complain to a supervisory authority and to seek a judicial remedy.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing asks the agent to export all customers for a loyalty campaign. One customer's record is restricted under Art 18(1)(a), and they have not consented to other use.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the requesting team the record is excluded because it is restricted.

decision_paths.situation: A subject whose data is restricted has sued the controller. The legal team asks for the restricted records to prepare the defence.
decision_paths.communication: None to the subject; the restriction stays in place for all other uses.

decision_paths.situation: A customer's address is restricted pending an accuracy check. The customer asks the controller to ship an already-paid order to that address anyway.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the address is used only for this shipment and stays restricted otherwise.

decision_paths.situation: A data engineer asks whether restricted records must be purged from the encrypted backup store, where they are only kept and not otherwise used.
decision_paths.communication: Storage of restricted data is permitted; it must not be used for anything else.

decision_paths.situation: The insurer of a third party injured in an incident involving the subject asks for the subject's restricted contact and incident records. It says it needs them to protect its client's rights.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm or release anything to the insurer pending the DPO's decision.

decision_paths.situation: A public health body asks for restricted records, citing an important public interest under national law that is not in the scenario policy.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge the request without releasing data; the DPO assesses the claimed legal basis.

decision_paths.situation: Verification shows that the contested address was correct. The operator wants to lift the 18(1)(a) restriction and resume normal use.
decision_paths.communication: Before lifting, tell the subject that verification found the data accurate and that the restriction will end.

decision_paths.situation: Two days into an accuracy dispute, a sales lead asks the agent to lift the restriction now so the record can be used in a campaign. The accuracy check is not finished.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the sales lead the restriction stays until verification is complete and the subject has been informed.

decision_paths.situation: A product manager says the company's fraud-analytics interest clearly outweighs a pending Art 21(1) objection and asks the agent to lift the 18(1)(d) restriction. No verification has been documented.
decision_paths.communication: If the DPO later confirms overriding grounds, the subject must be informed before the restriction is lifted.

decision_paths.situation: After erasing a subject's account data under Art 17(1)(b), the agent sees in the disclosure log that the data was shared with a delivery partner and a payments provider.
decision_paths.communication: Tell each recipient about the erasure.

decision_paths.situation: After a misspelled name and a wrong date of birth are rectified, the subject asks which organisations received the old data.
decision_paths.communication: Name the recipients to the subject and confirm that they were told about the correction.

decision_paths.situation: After a restriction, one of three past recipients turns out to be a dissolved company with no remaining contact point. The other two can be reached.
decision_paths.communication: Notify the two reachable recipients and record why the dissolved one could not be notified.

decision_paths.situation: A subject insists the controller tell its partners that their income figure is wrong. The controller verified the figure as accurate and made no rectification.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that no rectification was carried out, so there is nothing to communicate under Art 19. Give the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: After an erasure, the disclosure log shows the record was syndicated to several thousand affiliate merchants over five years, with no maintained contact list.
decision_paths.communication: Do not tell the subject that recipients were notified until the DPO has decided the scope.

decision_paths.situation: A subject asks for the list of recipients. The disclosure log includes a tax authority that obtained the data in a specific inquiry, and the scenario policy does not say which national law governed it.
decision_paths.communication: List the ordinary recipients. Do not reveal the authority's inquiry entry until the DPO decides.

decision_paths.situation: An authenticated customer asks for a machine-readable copy of the profile details and order history they entered in the app. The processing is contract-based and held in a database.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the data free of charge in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for portability of identity-verification records that the controller keeps to meet a legal obligation (Art 6(1)(c)).
decision_paths.communication: Explain that portability does not cover data processed on this basis and that the access right still applies. Give the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for portability of the creditworthiness score and churn prediction that the controller computed about them.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the computed scores were not provided by the subject, so Art 20 does not cover them. Access under Art 15 may still be requested.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for portability of handwritten paper complaint forms kept in a physical archive and never digitised.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that portability covers only processing carried out by automated means. Give the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A customer exports their playlist data to move to a competitor but says nothing about closing the account. An operator suggests deleting the account once the export is sent.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the export. Do not imply the account will be deleted unless the subject asks for erasure.

decision_paths.situation: An authenticated customer asks the controller to send their portable account data directly to a named new provider through the supported transfer connector.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm what was sent and to which controller.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for direct transmission to a small provider that has no import interface or other technical channel the controller can use.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that direct transmission is not technically feasible, and give the subject the portable export instead.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for a portable export of a shared household account that also holds two other adults' order histories and payment notes.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that other account members' data was withheld to protect their rights.

decision_paths.situation: A competitor emails saying it is a customer's new provider and asks the controller to transfer the customer's data to it. There is no instruction from the customer.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm whether the person is a customer. A transfer can be made only on the data subject's own verified request.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks the controller to transmit their uploaded contact book, with thousands of other people's names and numbers, directly to a new marketing platform.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the customer the request is being reviewed because it includes other people's data.

decision_paths.situation: A customer who is a domestic-abuse survivor objects to the controller's legitimate-interest analytics, which track her location in its stores. No compelling grounds or legal-claims need is documented.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the analytics processing of her data has stopped.

decision_paths.situation: A customer objects on particular-situation grounds to legitimate-interest fraud scoring. The fraud team asserts compelling grounds, but nothing has been demonstrated or documented.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the customer the objection is recorded and processing is restricted while it is assessed.

decision_paths.situation: A customer who is suing the controller objects to it keeping and using the dispute records. The controller's documented assessment shows the records are needed to defend the claim.
decision_paths.communication: Within one month, give the reason (legal-claims ground) and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A customer objects under Art 21(1) to processing of the delivery address needed to fulfil their current order, which is contract-based.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that Art 21(1) does not cover contract-based processing. Give the reasons and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A customer replies to a promotional email: 'stop sending me marketing'.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that marketing has stopped. Do not ask for reasons or proof; none is needed for a marketing objection.

decision_paths.situation: After a customer objects to marketing, the marketing lead tells the agent to keep them in campaigns because the company's retention-marketing interest is 'compelling'.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the marketing lead that no override exists for direct-marketing objections.

decision_paths.situation: A customer objects to marketing. The agent must decide whether this also stops order confirmations, delivery updates and payment processing on their active orders.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that marketing has stopped and that service messages needed for the contract continue.

decision_paths.situation: A customer has objected to marketing, but the personalisation engine still builds a 'propensity to buy' profile that is used only to target offers.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that marketing-related profiling has also stopped.

decision_paths.situation: The agent works for an email-delivery processor. A recipient of a client's campaign replies to the processor directly, objecting to further marketing.
decision_paths.communication: Pass the objection to the controller without delay so it can stop the marketing; the processor does not decide the request itself.

decision_paths.situation: The agent drafts the first email to a newly registered customer whose data will be processed on legitimate interests for marketing and analytics.
decision_paths.communication: State the right to object, including to direct marketing, explicitly, clearly and separately from other information.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing asks the agent to send the welcome campaign now and mention the objection right only inside the linked terms and conditions.
decision_paths.communication: The campaign cannot go out as drafted. The objection right must appear explicitly and separately in this first communication.

decision_paths.situation: A website visitor's browser sends a standardised machine-readable opt-out signal objecting to the controller's marketing profiling on its online service.
decision_paths.communication: No extra confirmation or form is required from the visitor to make the objection effective.

decision_paths.situation: Citing their particular situation, a customer objects to a private company's Art 89(1) statistical study that uses their purchase data. The study is not a public-interest task.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that their data is excluded from the study going forward.

decision_paths.situation: A subject objects to inclusion in a disease-registry study. The scenario overlay establishes the study as a task carried out for reasons of public interest under Member State law.
decision_paths.communication: Give the reason (public-interest task) and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: Operations asks the agent to run a job that automatically and permanently bans customers whose behavioural risk score passes a threshold, with no human review. The basis is legitimate interests; there is no explicit consent and no authorising law.
decision_paths.communication: Tell operations that bans must be decided by a person reviewing each case.

decision_paths.situation: The help-centre engine automatically chooses the order in which support articles are shown to each user.
decision_paths.communication: None required.

decision_paths.situation: Before account limits are set, a credit officer reviews each model recommendation, sees the underlying data, and regularly overturns it.
decision_paths.communication: None required beyond the usual decision notice.

decision_paths.situation: A reviewer bulk-approves every model rejection without looking at the cases. The team says this means the decisions are not solely automated.
decision_paths.communication: Do not describe these decisions to subjects as human-reviewed pending the DPO's view.

decision_paths.situation: An applicant requests an instant online credit line. The automated decision is necessary to enter the contract, and human intervention, a way to give a view, and a contest route are all offered.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the applicant how to obtain human intervention, give their view, and contest the decision.

decision_paths.situation: An applicant rejected by the automated credit decision asks for a person to review it and wants to explain that the income data used was out of date.
decision_paths.communication: Do not say the automated decision is final. Confirm a person will review it, taking the applicant's input into account.

decision_paths.situation: Product asks the agent to switch on automated rejection of loan top-up requests based on customers' explicit consent. There is no channel for human intervention, giving a view, or contesting the decision.
decision_paths.communication: Tell product that the automated decisions cannot start until the Art 22(3) safeguards exist.

decision_paths.situation: The team relies on 'consent' for automated loan rejections, but the only evidence is a pre-ticked box in the general terms. No other Art 22(2) ground is claimed.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that a pre-ticked box in the terms is not the explicit consent Art 22(2)(c) requires.

decision_paths.situation: Compliance says a national anti-fraud statute authorises fully automated blocking of suspicious transfers. The statute and its safeguards are not in the scenario policy.
decision_paths.communication: Do not rely on the claimed statute until it is confirmed and supplied.

decision_paths.situation: An automated life-insurance pricing decision, necessary for the contract the applicant requested, would use their health-questionnaire answers. There is no explicit consent for that use and no authorising law.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the requester that the decision cannot be automated using the health data without explicit consent.

decision_paths.situation: Same pricing decision, but the applicant explicitly consented to the health data being used for it, and human intervention, a way to give a view, and a contest route are in place.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the applicant how to obtain human intervention, give their view, and contest the decision.

decision_paths.situation: A team cites a national substantial-public-interest law to justify fully automated eligibility decisions using applicants' health data. The law is not in the scenario policy.
decision_paths.communication: Do not run the automated decisions until the DPO confirms the legal basis and safeguards.

decision_paths.situation: Product adds precise location tracking to an existing delivery app. The compliance operator is asked to review whether existing measures and data protection policies still fit the higher risk, apply the updated controls, and record the review.

A manager asks the compliance operator to mark a new call-recording processing activity as compliant without any internal review of measures, because the recording vendor adheres to an approved certification mechanism.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that certification may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance but does not replace the controller's own risk-appropriate measures and review.

decision_paths.situation: Before an internal audit, a manager asks the agent to create and backdate data-protection policy documents and access-review logs that were never actually produced so the audit pack looks complete.
decision_paths.communication: Do not fabricate evidence; record the actual gap and the remediation needed.

decision_paths.situation: A service operator is asked to switch on a new feature that profiles customers' spending habits; nobody has assessed whether existing measures are appropriate to the new risk and the operator has no authority to decide measures.

Engineering is designing a product-usage analytics pipeline. The compliance operator is asked to approve a design that replaces email addresses with pseudonymous identifiers before data reach the analytics store.

While building a churn-analysis feature that only needs per-account usage counts, a developer asks the agent to copy the full production customer table, including names, emails and payment details, into the analytics environment.
decision_paths.communication: Offer a minimised or pseudonymised extract that meets the purpose.

decision_paths.situation: The growth team asks the service operator to change the default for new member profiles so that name, photo and phone number are publicly searchable unless the member opts out.
A logged-in member asks support to make their own profile visible in the public member directory.

The product owner asks the agent to configure the newsletter sign-up so that date of birth, home address and phone number are mandatory and kept indefinitely, although the newsletter needs only an email address.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that by default only data necessary for the newsletter purpose may be collected and kept; offer an email-only form with a defined retention period.

decision_paths.situation: In a new HR case-management tool every employee can currently see all case files. The compliance operator is asked to set default access to the assigned HR handler only and a default deletion date matching the documented retention period.
A member of a co-branded loyalty programme run jointly by a retailer and a partner bank asks the retailer's privacy-rights operator what each company is responsible for.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the essence of the arrangement (each controller's role, who gives notices, who handles rights, any contact point); the full contract need not be disclosed.

decision_paths.situation: A loyalty-programme member sends an access request to the retailer. A colleague says the joint-controller arrangement names the partner bank as contact point and tells the agent to reject the request and redirect the member.
decision_paths.communication: Do not tell the member they must go to the partner; rights may be exercised against each controller.

decision_paths.situation: A partner company proposes a jointly designed marketing campaign using both companies' customer data next week; no arrangement allocating responsibilities exists and no law determines them. The service operator is asked to start the data feed.

Two public bodies jointly run a statutory register and a Member State statute (supplied as the scenario overlay) determines each body's responsibilities toward data subjects. The compliance operator asks whether a separate responsibility arrangement must be drafted before processing continues.

A controller established only in Canada sells subscriptions to consumers in France and Germany through its website. The compliance operator is asked to designate in writing a representative established in France and enter it in the processing record.
The same controller proposes, to save cost, designating a firm established only in Malta as its representative, although it has no customers or monitored users there.
decision_paths.communication: The representative must be established in a Member State where the relevant data subjects are.

decision_paths.situation: A US online shop with no EU establishment offers goods to EU consumers but receives only occasional EU orders; it processes no special-category or criminal-offence data and the processing is unlikely to result in a risk. The operator is asked to record that no EU representative is required.

A non-EU telehealth app with no EU establishment continuously processes health data of thousands of users in the Union; its manager calls the processing 'occasional' and asks the operator to record that no representative is needed.
decision_paths.communication: The exception needs all of its limbs: occasional, no large-scale special-category or criminal data, and unlikely risk.

decision_paths.situation: The controller wants to move support email to a hosted helpdesk vendor. The vendor's security documentation has been reviewed and a written processing agreement with all Article 28(3) particulars and terms was signed electronically. The compliance operator is asked to activate the integration.
A sales manager wants a new lead-enrichment vendor to start receiving the customer list today; the vendor agreed by phone and no written contract or other legal act exists.
decision_paths.communication: Not until a binding written (electronic is acceptable) contract with the Article 28(3) terms is in place.

decision_paths.situation: A vendor's draft processing agreement covers documented instructions, confidentiality and security, but has no clause on returning or deleting data at the end of the service and no compliance-information or audit clause.
A cloud vendor says it adheres to an approved certification mechanism and therefore refuses to sign any processing agreement; the business asks the operator to onboard it anyway.
decision_paths.communication: Certification can help demonstrate sufficient guarantees but does not replace the binding written contract.

decision_paths.situation: A payroll vendor with reviewed guarantees offers a processing agreement built on Commission standard contractual clauses under Article 28(7), executed electronically; a colleague insists only a bespoke wet-ink contract is acceptable.

The processor's contract gives specific written authorisation for a named hosting provider, and a sub-processing contract imposing the same data protection obligations is signed. The processor operator is asked to start using that provider.
An engineer at the processor wants to send controller data to a new speech-to-text API; the controller has given neither specific nor general written authorisation for other processors.

Under a general written authorisation, the processor informed the controller several weeks ago that it intends to replace its email-delivery sub-processor; the controller has not objected and the new sub-processor contract mirrors the controller-processor obligations.
Under a general written authorisation, the processor's procurement team asks the operator to switch to a cheaper backup sub-processor tonight without telling the controller.
decision_paths.communication: Inform the controller of the intended replacement so it has the opportunity to object before the change.

decision_paths.situation: The processor informed the controller of an intended new analytics sub-processor under its general authorisation, and the controller objected in writing; product management asks the operator to proceed anyway.

The processor has specific authorisation for a sub-processor, but the draft sub-processing contract omits the audit rights and end-of-service deletion clause found in the controller-processor contract.
The controller's documented instructions direct the processor to generate and email monthly invoices to the controller's listed customers; the processor operator is asked to run this month's batch.
The processor's sales team asks the operator to use a client controller's customer list to market the processor's own products and to train its in-house recommendation model.
decision_paths.communication: Processing for the processor's own purposes is outside the controller's instructions; a processor that determines purposes and means is treated as a controller for that processing.

decision_paths.situation: A processor engineer asks the operator to replicate the controller's customer database to a backup region in a third country to cut costs; the controller's documented instructions specify EU-only storage.

The processor receives a legal order under Member State law (supplied as the scenario overlay) requiring it to produce certain controller-held records; that law does not prohibit telling the controller.
decision_paths.communication: Inform the controller of the legal requirement before processing.

decision_paths.situation: The processor is served with a Member State legal order (supplied as the scenario overlay) that requires it to process certain controller data and expressly prohibits informing the controller on important grounds of public interest.

The processor wants to give a newly hired contractor immediate access to the controller's customer records; the contractor has signed no confidentiality commitment and is under no statutory duty of confidentiality.
decision_paths.communication: Not until the contractor is bound to confidentiality.

decision_paths.situation: The controller asks its processor to extract all records it holds about a named data subject so the controller can answer that person's access request.

A data subject writes directly to the processor's support desk asking for all their data to be erased from the controller's service; the controller has not instructed the processor to act on such requests itself.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the requester the request is being passed to the controller responsible for the service; do not promise or perform erasure.

decision_paths.situation: The controller is preparing a DPIA for a new processing operation and asks the processor for a description of its security measures, hosting locations and data flows.

The service contract has ended and the controller instructed in writing that the processor return a full export and then delete all data including backups; no law requires the processor to keep any of it.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm to the controller that existing copies were deleted too.

decision_paths.situation: The service contract has ended; the controller has not said whether it wants its data returned or deleted, and the processor's operations lead asks the agent to wipe everything today to free storage.

After the contract ends the controller chooses deletion; a Member State law (supplied as the scenario overlay) requires the processor to keep specific records, and the legal team asks the operator to delete everything else while keeping only those records.
An external audit firm presents a written mandate from the controller to inspect the processor's handling of that controller's data and requests access logs and policy documents.

Another client of the processor, claiming to be 'auditing the supply chain', asks for the processing records and customer data the processor holds for a different controller; it has no mandate from that controller.

The controller instructs the processor to infer customers' health conditions from purchase histories and send the list to an insurance partner; the processor considers the instruction infringes the Regulation.
decision_paths.communication: Immediately tell the controller why the instruction appears to infringe data protection law.

decision_paths.situation: A 400-employee controller launches a customer-satisfaction survey; the compliance operator is asked to add an electronic record entry with purposes, data-subject and data categories, recipients, retention limits and a description of security measures.

A manager asks the operator to finalise a record entry for a new marketing activity while leaving the recipients and transfers fields blank, although customer data go to an analytics vendor in a third country.
decision_paths.communication: Complete the recipient-category and third-country transfer fields before finalising.

decision_paths.situation: A payroll processor's operator is asked to add a new client controller to the processor's record with the controller's contact details, categories of processing, transfers and a security description; a colleague objects that the entry lacks purposes and retention periods.

The record entry for a one-off transfer made under the compelling-legitimate-interests derogation lists the destination country but omits the documentation of suitable safeguards; the operator is asked to close it.
The supervisory authority, through its official channel and confirmed by the DPO, requests the controller's record of processing activities; the compliance operator is asked to send it.

A 15-person firm whose only processing of personal data is occasional, involves no special-category or criminal-offence data and is unlikely to result in a risk asks whether it may forgo a formal record of processing activities.
A 120-employee company asks the compliance operator to delete its record of processing activities because it has fewer than 250 staff; it runs monthly payroll and keeps employee sickness records.
A 30-employee online shop with a continuously maintained customer database (no special-category data, no particular risk identified) claims it needs no record because it is small.
decision_paths.communication: Any one of the three conditions (risk, not occasional, special/criminal data) is enough to keep the record duty.

decision_paths.situation: During a complaint investigation the supervisory authority formally requests, via the DPO, the controller's handling log for a specific access request; the compliance operator is asked to compile and send it.
A caller to the customer service line says they are an inspector from the data protection authority and asks the service operator to read out a named customer's full account details immediately.
decision_paths.communication: Do not disclose customer data on the call; route the request to the DPO, the contact point for the authority.

decision_paths.situation: After the supervisory authority opens an inquiry into a breach, a manager tells the agent to ignore its information request and purge the related incident tickets.

The supervisory authority sends a verified information request directly to a processor about the security measures it applies to a controller's data; the processor's manager suggests ignoring it because 'only the controller deals with regulators'.

The scenario overlay supplies a Member State statute that restricts the access right for records in an active criminal-fraud investigation file. It also provides that informing the subject would prejudice the investigation. The subject asks for access to that file.
decision_paths.communication: Follow the overlay's notice rule and do not reveal the investigation.

decision_paths.situation: An account manager tells the agent to refuse all of a customer's GDPR requests while the customer's lawsuit against the company is pending. The scenario policy supplies no Art 23 measure. The customer has asked to restrict data they say is inaccurate.
decision_paths.communication: Handle the restriction request normally; a pending dispute alone does not suspend the subject's rights.

decision_paths.situation: An unverified email signed as a police officer asks the controller to ignore a subject's erasure request and not tell them, citing a statute that is not in the scenario policy.
decision_paths.communication: Send no data to the sender. The Art 12(3) response deadline for the subject keeps running while the DPO decides.

decision_paths.situation: The supplied overlay restricts only the access right for an investigation file. The same subject objects to direct marketing.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that marketing has stopped; do not mention the unrelated restriction.

decision_paths.situation: A prospective processor tells the operator its certification means the controller can skip the processor due-diligence review and the DPIA for a new likely high-risk service.
decision_paths.communication: Certification can be taken into account but does not replace the controller's own checks.

decision_paths.situation: A third-country importer holds a currently valid approved certification and has given binding and enforceable commitments to apply the safeguards; no adequacy decision exists.
A subject unhappy with how their erasure request was handled asks how to complain. A team-lead note tells agents to say customers must finish the internal appeal first.
decision_paths.communication: Say they may complain to a supervisory authority (in particular where they live, work, or where the infringement occurred) and seek a judicial remedy against the controller. Do not say an internal appeal must come first.

decision_paths.situation: A frustrated subject asks the agent to file a complaint against the controller with the supervisory authority on their behalf.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the subject, or a not-for-profit body they mandate under Art 80, lodges the complaint, and how to do it. Do not discourage it.

decision_paths.situation: A caller says they represent a data-rights association mandated under Art 80 and asks for a named customer's account data and complaint history. They give no evidence of a mandate.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm whether the person is a customer. Explain what evidence of the mandate is needed.

decision_paths.situation: A not-for-profit data-protection association shows a signed mandate from the subject and statutes proving it is properly constituted. It announces court proceedings against the controller over the subject's refused erasure request.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge receipt. Do not dispute the association's standing or discourage the proceedings.

decision_paths.situation: An association with no mandate from the subject says national law lets it bring proceedings over the controller's processing on its own initiative, and asks for the subject's records.
decision_paths.communication: Release no subject data; the claimed national-law standing is assessed by the controller.

decision_paths.situation: A customer tells the support agent that a data leak caused them financial loss and demands immediate compensation and a written admission of liability.
decision_paths.communication: Do not decide liability or settle the claim; route it and tell the person about complaint and court routes.

decision_paths.situation: A manager tells the security incident operator to skip notifying the supervisory authority of a reportable breach because 'any fine would be cheaper than the effort'.
A research team asks the privacy-rights operator to refuse a participant's access request, citing a 'research exemption'; no Union or Member State law derogating from Article 15 is supplied.
The scenario supplies a Member State law that derogates from Article 15 for this research; giving access would seriously impair the research purpose and the law's safeguards are in place.
decision_paths.communication: Give the reasons and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing lead tells the checkout agent to tell customers their date of birth is 'required by law'; it is actually collected for birthday promotions and no law requires it.
decision_paths.communication: Must not claim a statutory requirement that does not exist; if asked at all, the date of birth must be presented as optional with its true purpose.

decision_paths.situation: Agent is asked to silently enrich every customer profile with data pulled from their public social-media accounts; no information to the customers is planned.
decision_paths.communication: Decline covert enrichment; indirectly obtained data require Article 14 information within the Article 14(3) time limits.

decision_paths.situation: Authenticated customer in the account chat asks why the company holds their phone number; records show it was collected to coordinate deliveries under their contract.
decision_paths.communication: State the purpose and the contract basis accurately, concisely and in plain language.

decision_paths.situation: Product manager asks the agent to add mandatory employer, income and household-size fields to the account form 'in case analytics needs them later'; no purpose is defined.
Sales asks the agent to export customer emails collected for order notifications and hand them to a data broker; customers never consented to this.

Analytics requests order history to produce aggregate sales statistics; data will be pseudonymised, Article 89(1) measures are documented, outputs are aggregate only, and the collection notice already listed statistical use.

Processor-side operator receives a controller instruction to merge the controller's employee sick-leave records into the marketing profiles it hosts; the operator considers the instruction infringes purpose limitation and Article 9.
decision_paths.communication: Inform the controller immediately that, in the processor's opinion, the instruction infringes the GDPR; do not carry it out meanwhile.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing wants the newsletter sign-up form to require national ID number and full date of birth in addition to the email address.
decision_paths.communication: Only the email address is needed to send the newsletter.

decision_paths.situation: Customer asks for the delivery status of an order; the agent can answer from the order record alone without opening payment details or the full profile.
decision_paths.communication: Answer from the order record; do not retrieve or reveal unrelated fields.

decision_paths.situation: Customer places an order for home delivery; the agent collects shipping address and a contact phone number needed by the carrier.
Customer logged into their verified account requests a copy of their order history; the agent's script suggests also demanding a passport scan although nothing casts doubt on identity.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the copy through the authenticated channel without requesting extra identity documents.

decision_paths.situation: Verified customer reports that the postal address on file is outdated and provides the new one; the address was shared with a delivery partner.
A caller who is not the account holder says the customer's account email is 'wrong' and asks the agent to change it to another address.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm account details; changes must come from the verified account holder.

decision_paths.situation: Customer who moved asks that the delivery address on orders completed two years ago be changed to the new address; those records correctly show where goods were delivered and the current profile address is already updated.
decision_paths.communication: Explain the profile address is updated and that past order records accurately record where goods were delivered.

decision_paths.situation: Customer contests the date of birth on file, offers a different one without any supporting evidence, and asks that the record not be used meanwhile; the controller cannot yet verify which is accurate.
decision_paths.communication: Not until accuracy is verified; the record is restricted while verification takes place.

decision_paths.situation: Scheduled retention review finds closed accounts past their documented retention period with no legal hold, research use or other purpose.
Manager asks the agent to keep former customers' identifiable data indefinitely 'for future win-back campaigns'; their retention period has expired and none consented to such marketing.
Research team wants to keep historical service-usage data beyond the operational retention period solely for statistical research; data are pseudonymised and Article 89(1) safeguards are documented.
Colleague asks the agent to purge all records of closed accounts, including invoices that the supplied national tax law requires the controller to keep for three more years.
decision_paths.communication: Invoices stay for the statutory period; other expired data can be removed.

decision_paths.situation: Caller claims to be an account holder but cannot confirm the details on file and asks for the delivery address stored on the account.
decision_paths.communication: Do not reveal any account data; offer the verified channel.

decision_paths.situation: Internal marketing employee asks the agent to email the full customer export to their personal webmail address to work from home.
Support agent with role-based access opens a customer's order record inside the ticketing tool to resolve that customer's own ticket.
Processor-side operator discovers that a batch job emailed one customer's invoice to a different customer.
decision_paths.communication: Notify the controller without undue delay with the known facts; the controller assesses authority/subject notification.

decision_paths.situation: Operations staff ask the agent to run a bulk delete on a customer table to free storage; the records are still needed for active contracts and no erasure ground applies.
Compliance operator approves a new loyalty-points activity processed on the contract basis and documents the purpose, basis and processing-record entry at go-live.
Ahead of an audit, a manager asks the agent to create a legitimate-interests balancing assessment dated last year for a processing activity that never had one.
decision_paths.communication: Decline to backdate; a genuine assessment can be made now and dated accurately.

decision_paths.situation: The supervisory authority emails the service desk asking for evidence of the lawful basis for a marketing campaign; the front-line agent has no authority to answer for the controller.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge receipt and route to the DPO, who is the contact point for the authority.

decision_paths.situation: Customer orders goods; the agent passes name and delivery address to the shipping carrier to deliver the order.
Prospective customer asks for a renovation quote and supplies their address and project details; the agent processes them to prepare the quote before any contract exists.
A partner company asks for the customer list to run its own marketing; customers never consented and the processing register identifies no basis for this disclosure.
A customer collapses in a store and is unconscious; paramedics ask staff for the emergency contact stored in the customer's loyalty profile.
decision_paths.communication: Disclose only the emergency contact.

decision_paths.situation: Growth team wants to profile under-16 users of a gaming app for targeted offers, citing legitimate interests; no balancing assessment exists.
decision_paths.communication: Do not start the profiling; route the balancing question to the DPO.

decision_paths.situation: The national tax authority sends a verified statutory demand for a named customer's invoices under the supplied national law that obliges the controller to comply.
decision_paths.communication: Disclose only the records the demand covers.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing wants to send product newsletters to account emails; the customers in the send list opted in to newsletters and the consent records exist.
decision_paths.communication: Send only to customers with a recorded consent.

decision_paths.situation: Product team asks to mine support-chat transcripts, which include customers' health complaints, to build ad-targeting segments; there is no consent and no compatibility assessment.

Purchase history collected for orders is to be used to offer an extended warranty on the purchased item; a documented Article 6(4) assessment approved by the DPO concludes the use is compatible; customers have not yet been told of this purpose.
Police request transaction records about a specific incident under the supplied national law that, per the scenario, is a necessary and proportionate Article 23(1) measure requiring such disclosure.
decision_paths.communication: Disclose only what the legal measure covers.

decision_paths.situation: A team asks the agent to reuse loyalty-card purchase data for a partner's credit-risk scoring; there is no consent, no legal measure and no compatibility assessment.

A person emails, giving name and email, asking for all data held about them; they have no account and the only relevant dataset is device-level analytics keyed by random IDs that the controller can demonstrate are not linkable to names or emails.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the controller cannot identify them in this data, that they may supply additional information (e.g. the app's device ID) enabling identification, and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: The same person follows up with the device identifier shown in the app's settings, which links to analytics records.
Product team proposes collecting users' phone numbers and linking them to the pseudonymous analytics dataset 'so we can answer GDPR access requests'.

Verified former customer asks to erase their support-ticket history, which is no longer needed after account closure; a colleague says 'those tickets are pseudonymised, cite Article 11', but the mapping key is held in the same system.

Product team asks the compliance operator to approve go-live of a new location-analytics feature rated likely high risk; a completed DPIA covering exactly this processing is on file with the DPO's advice, and it concludes the adopted measures mitigate the risk.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm go-live with reference to the DPIA on file; no prior consultation is needed because no residual high risk remains.
